task: Build a new freelance finance tracking app: Python FastAPI backend with PostgreSQL, React+Vite frontend, JWT auth, receipt image upload, mileage entry, dashboard summary, tax-ready PDF/CSV export. Includes unit and integration tests.

issues: Protected endpoints (receipts, dashboard, export, etc.) return 401 Unauthorized because JWT tokens cannot be decoded. The token is created with an 'exp' claim as a datetime object, which the python-jose library fails to verify, causing a JWTError during decoding. This breaks authentication for all routes that depend on `get_current_user`.
The UI primary flow also fails because the backend does not accept the JWT token after registration/login, leading to 401 errors when fetching the dashboard summary.
review.feedback: Update the JWT creation to store the expiration claim as a numeric timestamp (int) instead of a datetime object. This will allow python-jose to correctly verify the token during decoding. In `backend/app/auth.py`, modify `create_access_token` to set `exp` using `int(expire.timestamp())`. After the change, all protected routes should accept the token, fixing the failing tests and UI flow.

stalled: acceptance tests failed 5 rounds in a row with: FAIL: GET /receipts returned N, body: {"detail":"Could not validate credentials"}

security.summary: Skipped until tests and validation pass.

ui.summary: The UI largely respects the design tokens and passes automated accessibility (axe) checks, but critical user‑experience gaps break the primary flow. The Dashboard does not handle a 401 response correctly – it shows an error banner instead of the expected empty‑state copy and prevents auto‑login after registration. Authentication tokens are not reliably persisted or attached to API calls, causing repeated unauthorized errors. Several spec‑defined states (loading spinners, empty/ error messages, success toasts) are missing or mis‑implemented in forms and export actions. Form accessibility is incomplete: labels are omitted or placed incorrectly, autocomplete attributes and password visibility toggles are absent, and field‑level validation feedback is not shown. Navigation is generally present but not guaranteed on every signed‑in screen (e.g., Export screen). Overall the code uses the design tokens correctly (no ad‑hoc colors), focus styling is applied globally, and there are no obvious unused class names, but the functional and usability deficiencies are high‑severity and must be addressed before the product can be considered polished.

findings.issue: Dashboard does not handle a 401 Unauthorized response; it displays an error banner "Failed to load data. Retry." instead of auto‑redirecting to login or showing the empty‑state copy "No data yet. Add a receipt or mileage to get started." causing the primary flow to break.
findings.fix: Add error handling for 401: clear stored token, redirect to the sign‑in page, and on a successful fetch with no data render the empty state UI with the exact copy and a CTA button. Ensure the empty state is also shown when the API returns an empty list.

findings.issue: Authentication token from /auth/register (auto‑login) is not stored or attached to subsequent requests, leading to 401 errors on the dashboard summary call.
findings.fix: Persist the access_token (e.g., in localStorage or a secure http‑only cookie) after registration/login, and include it in the Authorization header for all API calls. Implement a token refresh or graceful fallback to the login screen on token expiry.

findings.issue: Login form lacks visible <label> elements above inputs, missing autocomplete attributes (email, current‑password), and does not provide a password show/hide toggle or password‑rules hint. Inline field error messages are not rendered.
findings.fix: Add <label htmlFor="email">Email</label> and <label htmlFor="password">Password</label> above the inputs, set autocomplete="email" and autocomplete="current-password", include a button to toggle password visibility, display password requirements under the field, and render field‑level error messages from API validation.

findings.issue: Register form does not show labels above the password and confirm‑password fields, lacks autocomplete="new-password", and does not display password‑rule guidance or inline validation errors for email, password mismatch, etc.
findings.fix: Add visible labels for Email, Password, Confirm password, set appropriate autocomplete attributes, show the password rule hint ("8+ characters, at least one number, one uppercase letter"), and render inline error messages under each field when validation fails.

findings.issue: Submit button is disabled silently during upload and does not replace its label with a loading spinner. Inline field errors are not displayed; error banners are used instead of field‑level feedback.
findings.fix: When the form is submitting, set aria‑disabled="true" on the button, replace its label with the <LoadingSpinner/> component, and keep the button size unchanged. Show inline validation messages beneath each offending input using the .error class and ARIA attributes (aria-invalid, aria-describedby).

findings.issue: Similar to receipt upload: loading state hides the button label without a spinner, and field‑level validation messages are missing.
findings.fix: Implement the same loading spinner replacement and inline error display logic as described for the receipt form.

findings.issue: Export PDF/CSV buttons lack tooltips/aria‑labels describing their purpose, and when an export is in progress the button does not show a spinner or become disabled.
findings.fix: Add aria‑label or native tooltip with the copy from the spec (e.g., "Download a PDF ready for tax filing"), disable the button during the request, and replace its text with a <LoadingSpinner/> while showing a success toast on completion.

findings.issue: Primary navigation (HeaderNav on desktop, BottomNav on mobile) is not rendered on the Export screen, leaving the user without a persistent navigation element.
findings.fix: Wrap the Export component with the Layout component that includes the navigation bar, ensuring consistent navigation across all signed‑in screens.

findings.issue: Custom modal dialogs do not have explicit focus‑trap implementation; while :focus-visible outlines appear, keyboard users may tab out of the dialog.
findings.fix: Implement a focus‑trap (e.g., using a library like focus-trap-react) so that focus stays within the modal until it is closed, and return focus to the triggering element on close.

findings.issue: File input does not have an accessible description (e.g., supported formats, max size) linked via aria-describedby.
findings.fix:
Add a

Supported formats: JPG, PNG, PDF. Max size 5 MB.

and associate it with the .

findings.issue: No unused CSS classes detected (styles.rules=15, classes=2, unmatchedCount=0), but the .error class is defined and may not be used in some forms.
findings.fix: Audit the usage of .error; if unused, remove it to keep CSS lean.

findings.issue: Form fields and labels are aligned vertically without a consistent grid system, leading to inconsistent spacing and alignment.
findings.fix: Implement a grid-based layout with consistent vertical and horizontal spacing for all form elements.

findings.issue: Typography lacks a type scale; all text appears to use the same font size and weight, with no visual hierarchy.
findings.fix: Apply a type scale: use larger, bold font for the heading; medium weight for labels; smaller size for placeholder text or error messages.

findings.issue: No error states or validation feedback shown — the design spec requires inline error messages for invalid inputs.
findings.fix: Add inline error messages below each field when validation fails, using consistent styling and color.

findings.issue: The 'Create account' button is visually distinct but lacks subtle affordance or feedback (e.g., hover state, loading indicator) that would indicate it's the primary action.
findings.fix: Add hover state, loading spinner, and disabled state to the button to reinforce its primary action status.

findings.issue: The form fields are not touch-friendly — they are too close to the edges and lack sufficient padding for finger taps.
findings.fix: Increase padding around input fields and ensure they are spaced adequately for finger interaction.

findings.issue: The layout is not optimized for desktop — fields are stacked vertically and hug the left edge, lacking the spacious, columnar layout expected for desktop.
findings.fix: Reorganize form into a responsive grid on desktop, with fields arranged in columns and appropriate spacing.

findings.issue: visual quality 5/10 on 'sign-up' (needs 8+): The sign-up screen is functionally complete but lacks visual polish and design sophistication. It uses browser-default styling with no custom type scale or spacing, and the layout feels like a placeholder. The form is vertically aligned but not grid-based, and the button is touch-friendly but the overall presentation is unremarkable and uninspired for a polished product.
findings.fix: Address this screen's findings until it looks polished and professional.

went_well: The planner created a coherent high‑level architecture and the designer produced a detailed UI flow (ui_flow.json) and a component inventory.
The coder scaffolded a working FastAPI backend with JWT authentication and PostgreSQL models, and the internal FastAPI tests passed once the auth bugs were fixed.
The vision agent rendered UI screens, allowing the UI validator to check visual flow and giving the reviewers concrete evidence of UI state.

improvements.title: Make Ruff lint warnings non‑blocking
improvements.evidence: Rounds 1 and 2 list "validator: ruff" as a failing validator. The output shows dozens of F401 "imported but unused" warnings (e.g., "backend/app/auth.py:2:8: F401 `secrets` imported but unused"). Reviewer notes these are merely warnings, yet they stopped progress.
improvements.change: Edit static validator (validate.py) for Ruff: run `ruff check --ignore=F401` or filter out F401 messages, and remove Ruff from the mandatory blocker list. Only treat syntax/runtime errors (E‑codes) as fatal.
improvements.expected_effect: Removes a blocker that fired in 2 of 8 rounds, cutting dozens of coder turns that were spent merely cleaning imports and speeding up each round by ~10‑15 minutes.

improvements.title: Auto‑generate missing UI backend configuration
improvements.evidence: Validator "ui backend config" blocked rounds 1 and 2 with the message "This app has a backend but no ui‑backend.json ... Write ui‑backend.json at the app root ...". The coder had to add this file manually, consuming several turns.
improvements.change: Add a pipeline step after the designer that checks for the presence of `ui-backend.json`. If absent, write the file automatically using the template provided in the validator message. Alternatively, modify ui_check.mjs to treat a missing file as a warning and auto‑create it.
improvements.expected_effect: Eliminates the early UI‑backend config failure, allowing UI flow validation to start in the first round and saving roughly 3‑5 coder turns per run.

improvements.title: Standardise and auto‑fix TypeScript configuration
improvements.evidence: Validator "typescript (tsc)" blocked 7 of 8 rounds. Errors include "Cannot use JSX unless the '--jsx' flag is provided" (round 1), "error TS17004" for missing JSX, and "error TS6133: 'token' is declared but its value is never read" (round 8). Many stem from an incomplete or malformed tsconfig (e.g., missing "jsx" and invalid "moduleResolution").
improvements.change: Extend the designer prompt to require a correct `tsconfig.json` (include "jsx": "react-jsx", proper "include" patterns, and a supported "moduleResolution"). Add a post‑design hook that writes a default tsconfig if the file is missing or invalid. Also relax the TypeScript validator to only block on syntax errors, not on missing compiler options, and auto‑inject defaults when possible.
improvements.expected_effect: Reduces TypeScript validation failures from most rounds to only genuine syntax problems, cutting the bottleneck that halted the pipeline for >1 hour per round.

improvements.title: Raise coder turn limit and adjust repeat‑failure guard
improvements.evidence: Coder hit its turn limit in rounds 1, 2, 5 and 6 (see "coder_turn_limit": true). Those rounds also had the most validator blocks, meaning the coder was cut off before fixing all issues. Round 6 was the slowest (4351 s) partly because the coder ran out of turns early.
improvements.change: Increase `coder_turn_limit` from its current value to at least 500 turns per round, or make it dynamic (e.g., allow +200 turns for each additional blocking validator). Modify the repeat‑failure guard to allow more iterations when the same validator keeps failing (e.g., JWT token handling).
improvements.expected_effect: Gives the coder enough iterations to resolve complex multi‑file issues in a single round, preventing artificial stalls and reducing total runtime by ~15‑20 %.

improvements.title: Provide concrete, actionable reviewer guidance for JWT handling
improvements.evidence: From round 4 to round 8 the reviewer repeatedly flags "Frontend API client does not attach the JWT token" and similar messages, but the coder only partially addressed the problem (e.g., declared `token` but never used). The feedback remained high‑level, leading to six rounds of repeated UI primary‑flow failures.
improvements.change: Rewrite the reviewer prompt to require a concrete remediation step whenever missing authentication is detected: include a short code snippet that stores `response.data.access_token` in `localStorage` and sets `axios.defaults.headers.common['Authorization'] = 'Bearer ' + token`. Also add a rule that, when a JWT‑related validator fails, the reviewer must suggest the exact file/method to edit.
improvements.expected_effect: Delivers precise actionable guidance, enabling the coder to fix token storage and header injection in one go, which should eliminate the recurring 401 errors and collapse the acceptance‑test failure streak after the next round.
